name: The People Paris Marais
detail: Newly built ! Facility was great and the staffs was kind.

name: St Christopher's Inn Paris - Gare du Nord
detail: I arrived at Gare du Nord train station, Paris from the CDG airport (easy - phew!) and found that St Christopher's Inn was easy to find once you navigated yourself out of the station and found your bearings on Rue de Dunkurque (walk towards the post office). Although I arrived early they were very friendly and offered me a shower to freshen up and (paid) lockers to hold my stuff until 2pm check in. If you forget anything like a towel (whoops!), you can rent one for the length of your stay as well as buy other basic essentials. I found the staff very informative, spoke English well and tried their best to accommodate my every need. The room (6 mixed dorm) and bed linen were really clean (amazing doona!), warm and secure. You also got a massive drawer to lock your stuff in under your bunk. The showers were good but the cleaning agent/or disinfectant in the showers/communal bathroom was pretty stinky?! I also found it difficult to keep pressing the shower button whilst having a shower due to a neurological disorder in my arm but I managed. They were of a decent size so you could get changed in the cubicle without getting your clothes wet. The food at night was good (I'm a vegetarian - burger pattie was really dry) but not fantastic. The continental breakfast was on the other hand great and good quality! Baguettes, cheese, cereal, coffee, juice, etc. nice. I also used the laundry facilities up stairs (about 5 Euro wash and dry), which was good. Overall my stay there was great and will stay there again en route back to Oz. Can't really fault anything of locker, towel rent and laundry costs as well as stinky bathrooms but otherwise the location is pretty darn awesome! Thanks guys and gals. Looking forward to seeing you all again!! Oh and the free day tour with Roberta through Paris is so worth it!! Just rug up and don't drink too much coffee beforehand (no toilets!! ha!).

name: Villa Montparnasse Hotel
detail: Arriving at the height of July summer afternoon heat, the rapid check in by proficient staff, and the clean shower and the effective air conditioning made this hotel a welcome respite. The renovation work was effective, including decor with solid wood furniture, quality drapes and bedding, and updated bathroom fixtures. The showerhead bracket was loose requiring use of the inconvenient handheld hose with shower barrier inadequate to keep water within the bath. Location was ideal, two blocks from the RER line direct from Paris CDG airport, and one block from a pedestrian side-street lined with grocery, bakery, speciality food and restaurants where it is possible to economize on food rather than the hotel meals. Public WIFI connection in the lobby was adequate, but plan ahead as there is only a single lobby electrical outlet to recharge laptops. We found the $160 Agoda high-season price a bit high, but within the four-start market value range in this area of Paris.

name: The People Paris Nation
detail: I would stay here again if I return to Paris, I love France.

name: Enjoy Hostel
detail: Pictures really unrealistic. Corona regulations not respected - masks only worn sometimes. one of the rooms is adjoined to another and therefore you have to walk through 1 room to get to another room. no elevator. kitchen was constantly dirty. 'free breakfast' = baguette with jam or butter plus coffee (same breakfast everyday.) Staff don't speak English (quite rude with the 'pas Anglais' attitude sometimes. one of the rooms was leaking (the a/c) and it wasn't fixed only mopped and towels (upon several requests) were brought. I was happy that they kept my bags for me. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

name: The People - Paris Bercy
detail: I realy had a wonderful time while staying in here. Paris is a beautiful city and this hostel is amazing. Staff are all friendly. Shout out to bartender and the reception while I am check in and check out. Exceptional. Although I stayed in mix dorm, privacy is still number 1. The bathroom and restroom available in each room. The bed, the heater, and the rooftop are the best. Easy to find breakfast if you want to explore more, since in front of hostel, there's market/flea market, and this hostel located near the monoprix supermarket! Sounds so amazing and perfect..

name: JO&JOE Paris Gentilly
detail: From what I understood the hostel isn't located in Paris city, however in Paris area, so be careful with what kind of metro tickets you buy. However, generally no problem with that, as there's a metro station a couple of meters away and you can easily get wherever in Paris you need. The hostel in itself is incredible, all in neon lights, there's a roof terrace with a bar, as well as a bar downstairs for your morning coffee, which you can enjoy in a beautiful patio chill area. The staff is very nice and always very helpful. Had the best stay. I had the cabin , which gives you your own personal space,and the price for that is amazingly good; there's enough toilets/showers for everyone, never had to wait. Basically, when I visit Paris again, I'm definitely staying here. Merci Jo&Joe, c'etait une experience incroyable :)

name: St Christopher's Inn Paris - Canal
detail: The reception is usually always pretty busy but that's a good sign. The free buffet style breakfast is great for getting an early start on your day to see Paris' attractions easily accessible from the Pink line just a short 5-8 minute walk from the hostel along the canal. If you walk a little more there's gorgeous parks where you can sit and picnic overlooking the Science museum. Later at night, grab a drink at the bar right in the lobby and continue your after party like I did with friends from around the globe drinking strange liquor that the Argentinian girl brought from back home. Overall, this Hostel was a pleasant experience. Would recommend.
